An Organization's Introduction to eLearning and Platform Selection

Do you need an LMS? Maybe one day, but you probably don't need to decide now.

If you're on the fence, odds are good you're not a school system or IHE, and you may not need one at all.

Take the 30-second self-assessment ↓
↓
01 · Common myths

Starting around 2020, when pandemic closures sent many professional learning organizations into asynchronous delivery, platforms built for schools felt necessary for any nonprofit trying to reach external audiences or internal staff. It turns out those platforms are often:

  • Expensive: per-seat pricing adds up quickly and makes "cost of ownership" a tricky variable.
  • Not a great fit: enterprise LMS focus on capturing grades and credit requirements while integrating with a district or university's student information. Nonprofits rarely need or care.
  • Compliance driven: built around requirements for learners, not flexibly engaging professionals or volunteers.

Our team has supported over a dozen nonprofits delivering professional development internally and externally, and we've learned to ask a few questions we'll share with you below. When you're ready, we offer a platform selection service. But we think it's best to start by delivering some learning modules to your intended audience.

Common myths
Tap the card to flip it: the myth on the front, what's actually true on the back.
Myth
tap to flip
Actually
tap to flip back
  1. You can deliver most learning assets online, including eLearning modules, to a targeted group of learners without an enterprise LMS.
  2. That's backwards. Publish, pilot, and learn about your business requirements before committing to a platform.
  3. Building courses in an LMS is how you get locked in. Build learning assets in universal file types with authoring tools, not an LMS, and take them with you from platform to platform as you grow.
  4. Authoring tools make assets and modules of learning. Platforms host them. See the metaphors below to disentangle the two.
  5. SCORM is an industry-standard file type that works in most enterprise LMS, but you can pilot and publish eLearning without it. Web hosting and xAPI are options to explore depending on your requirements.
  6. Content built in universal formats works on whatever platform you pick later. Start building now.
  7. Platforms don't create engagement; relevant, well-designed learning does. Adoption is a design problem, not a hosting problem.
  8. "Free" platforms shift costs to admin time, hosting, and support, and they still shape your content around their structure.
  9. Small orgs benefit most from portable modules. A handful of PDFs, videos, and web modules can serve a whole network without any platform.
  10. If your assets are in universal formats, moving is a weekend, not a rebuild. Lock-in comes from where you build, not where you host.

Confused by any of these terms? Read on. Already know them and want to jump to a self-assessment?

02 · The landscape

How the pieces connect

Expertise goes in. Universal formats come out. Platforms come last, and audiences connect through them. Flip any card between 🏠 and 🎵.

1
Expertise (the input)
Every learning program starts with what your organization already knows: the experts, practitioners, and leaders who hold the content.
SMEsstaffpartnersacademicspractitionersexperts in the field
🏠 How you live: what you need from a room, a piece of furniture, a home. You bring that knowledge; the builders bring the craft.
🎵 The musicians. No catalog or streaming deal matters without the talent. Your experts are the band.

The software where assets get made. You don't live in them; you build in them.

File types that keep your assets portable across any platform. We recommend clients build in these first.

Platforms
Where learners access learning: an LMS, a knowledge hub, or your own website. The biggest commitment, and usually the most deferrable one.
per-learner pricinglong license termscostly integrations
🏠 The house. Committing early is signing a mortgage before you know your family size. And built-ins don't move.

6
Your audience
The learners you reach through the platform. And it runs both ways: learners add information, and courses personalize around them. Learn how they engage before you commit to where.
🏠 The neighborhood: the community, habitat, and infrastructure the house connects to. That's what you're really choosing.
🎵 The fanbase. You find them where they already listen, and your first releases teach you who they really are.
03 · The trap

The lock-in trap

Don't lock into a platform until you know how your audience will use it. Platforms often charge per learner, bind you to multi-year licenses, and require costly integration with your other systems. A pilot answers the questions a contract can't:

What's the market? Desktop or mobile? Who's the customer? When & how do they use it?

Skip the lock-in: get learning assets in front of your audience as a trial, test, or pilot, and learn.

Client stories
04 · Build portable

Build in universal formats first

Assets built this way snap together like Lego, into different courses for different audiences, and move from platform to platform when you finally choose (or build) your home.

An LMS
when tracking matters
A knowledge hub
when reference matters
Your website
when reach matters

The same assets work in all three. That's the point.

05 · Self-assessment

So, do you need an LMS?

Two honest questions. Thirty seconds.

QUESTION 1 OF 2
Do you have a hard requirement today for tracking completions, certifications, or compliance reporting?
QUESTION 2 OF 2
Do you already know your audience: their devices, their habits, and how many of them there are?
YOU'RE READY
Shop for an LMS, carefully.
Negotiate short initial terms, confirm SCORM import and export, and keep every asset in universal formats so the platform serves you, not the other way around.
Start over
GOOD NEWS: YOU CAN WAIT
Pilot first. Decide later.
Launch a few learning modules in universal formats to gauge business requirements, adoption, and user behavior. Let real usage data, not a sales demo, pick your platform.
Start over
